sample_unit: held-out test cases (patients) from whole-body FDG PET/CT

links.outcome: Performance on external-site test cases versus internal cases, including clinician Likert ratings
links.effect: Improved competency metric by +20.4 on external set; mean Likert 4.00 internal vs 4.17 external, indicating maintained performance under site shift among 276 external cases.
links.quote: RIDE achieves the strongest overall drafting performance and cross-site generalization, improving a clinically grounded competency metric by +20.4 on the external set and maintaining high clinician ratings under shift (mean Likert 4.00 internal; 4.17 external) while also delivering the best TNM staging performance among evaluated baselines.

unlisted_practices: Decomposing report drafting into structured TNM-oriented impressions followed by organ-wise exemplar retrieval and LLM synthesis

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates RIDE, a two-stage multimodal AI framework for drafting PET/CT reports, tested via automated metrics and clinician ratings on retrospective multi-center datasets.
